metadata.name: keys
metadata.description: the SHIPPED defaults roster — =kvseed copies any name missing from usercfg (never overwriting a user row). refreshApps stomps this segment freely; that is the point: new shipped keys flow in, user values stand.

metadata.name: supabase_url
metadata.description: the default Supabase project URL (public). sb.default derives from the usercfg row this seeds — edit the row in the ⚙ config view.

metadata.name: supabase_anonkey
metadata.description: the default Supabase publishable anon key (public — browser-safe by design; the only secret is the per-user JWT, which lives in the session store behind a SecretHandle).

metadata.name: B1
metadata.description: the ⚙ CONFIG view: the usercfg kv sheet — the persistent user-specific key-value surface (public config ONLY, never tokens). Rows are real usercfg.* cels; the composer row (name + value + ➕) mints new keys via kv.mint. Ships in the BOOTSTRAP form — B5's =kvseed splices the live row references on every open (and re-splices after a refreshApps reverts this formula).

metadata.name: sb.default
metadata.description: THE default Supabase project config, DERIVED from the usercfg kv sheet rows (edit them in the ⚙ config view) — owned by the 👤 Profile doc; chat/data docs reference it, they never define it.

metadata.name: B2
metadata.description: the LOGIN view: signed out it renders the email/password card (grok.signin → supabase-auth → tokens into the session store); signed in it becomes the session card (who you are + Sign out). Every chat/data doc gates on signedIn(sb.default.auth) — sign in HERE once.

cels.f: =view('🔐 login', loginpane({project: 'default', authed: signedIn(sb.default.auth), email: grok.email, password: grok.password, status: grok.status, session: sb.default.auth}))

metadata.name: B3
metadata.description: the IDENTITY WALLET view (keystore): create/unlock the sealed keypair, reshuffle, change passcode, export/import the keystore file, recovery phrase. Private keys live module-scope inside keystore — no key material ever reaches a cel; formulas may reference only keystore.status/name/identity.

cels.f: =view('👤 wallet', profileui(keystore.status, keystore.name, keystore.identity, profile.p1, profile.p2, profile.nm, profile.imp, profile.msg, profile.phrase))

metadata.name: B4
metadata.description: a visible probe of the NON-SECRET auth status cel ({status, email, userId}) — what other sheets are allowed to see of your session. The JWT itself is not here and cannot be referenced from any formula.

metadata.name: B5
metadata.description: the DEFAULTS-MERGE rule, as a visible cell: copy any usercfg_defaults row missing from usercfg (a user's edited value is NEVER overwritten; deleting a row = reset-to-default on the next open). usercfg is install:'once' — refreshApps stomps only the defaults segment and this doc, so user config survives a factory refresh while NEW shipped keys still flow in.

manifests.name: usercfg_defaults
manifests.description: the SHIPPED usercfg defaults (supabase url/anonkey rows + roster). Stomped freely by refreshApps — =kvseed merges missing names into the user-owned usercfg on every open, never overwriting a user row.

manifests.name: usercfg
manifests.description: the persistent user-specific key-value sheet (kvsheet rows = real cels; PUBLIC config only — tokens live in the session store, never cels). Ships EMPTY with install:'once': the first open seeds it from usercfg_defaults via =kvseed, and refreshApps NEVER re-puts it — user rows survive a factory refresh; new shipped keys merge in (missing names only).

manifests.name: identity
manifests.description: 👤 Profile (a sheetapp document) — identity + sign-in as visible cells: the usercfg segment is the persistent user key-value sheet (public config only; supabase url/anonkey rows seed it), B1 =view ⚙ config (kvsheet over usercfg — the composer row adds new keys), sb.default ={url:…, anonkey:…} derives from those rows, B2 =view login (loginpane → tokens into the session store behind a SecretHandle; once the wallet is unlocked the refresh token persists as a wallet-wrapped OPFS sidecar, so unlocking the wallet restores your sessions), B3 =view wallet (keystore), B4 the non-secret auth-status probe.
